response.rationale: C1 is the only candidate directly anchored to the ictal EEG: rhythmic right frontal epileptiform discharges are time-locked to the recurrent paroxysmal dizziness, vertigo and dull response, explaining the brief episodes with impaired awareness and left arm shaking. R1 and R5 rely on dizziness/vertigo but lack an EEG correlate and are contradicted by absent posterior circulation/brainstem changes and absent brainstem signs. R2 is nonspecific blood pressure elevation without a seizure correlate. R4 is the same diagnosis without the right frontal localization, so it is a less complete correlated restatement.

rejected.why: Paroxysmal dizziness, vertigo and left arm shaking are nonspecific; the EEG time-locked epileptiform discharge pattern makes a purely transient ischemic cause unlikely.
Same epileptic syndrome as C1 but lacks the anatomical right frontal localization supplied by the EEG discharge origin.
Dizziness and vertigo are compatible, but the absence of focal brainstem signs and posterior circulation/brainstem MRI changes argues against vertebrobasilar insufficiency.
Blood pressure is elevated, but there is no paroxysmal EEG correlate and the episode semiology is better explained by focal seizures.
